articles.title: Medical Devices; Gastroenterology-Urology Devices; Classification of the Flushing and Storage Solution for Vascular Autografts at Room Temperature
articles.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying the flushing and storage solution for vascular autografts at room temperature into class II (special controls). The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the flushing and storage solution for vascular autografts at room temperature. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.

Electronic Logging Device Requirements: Application for Exemption; Federation of Professional Truckers
articles.summary: FMCSA announces its decision to deny the application from the Federation of Professional Truckers (FOPT) requesting an exemption from the electronic logging device (ELD) requirements. FOPT requests an exemption to allow professional drivers the option to record their records of duty status (RODS) manually, instead of using an ELD. Analysts expect few breakthroughs as trade tensions simmer. China rejects worries about its exports and criticism of overcapacity, seen as unfairly driving down prices by flooding markets. articles.content: Chartering’s AI revolution brings competitive edge back to people - Splash247 Splash Singapore The paradox confronting modern chartering desks is becoming increasingly clear: the more data and technology everybody gets, the harder it becomes to differentiate. That was one of the central themes to emerge from the Chartering Spotlight at last week’s Splash Singapore, where charterers, operators and technology providers debated how AI, transparency and increasingly sophisticated data are changing the fixing process — while repeatedly returning to the importance of judgement, relationships and experience. Torbjørn Gjervik, CEO of Western Bulk, said the proliferation of common platforms means competing desks increasingly reach remarkably similar conclusions. “We all use basically the same two, three platforms,” he said. “Quite often we experience that we are pricing stuff within a few cents of each other.” The differentiator, he argued, is how the information is interpreted. “The digital tool is great to have. It’s a necessity, but it can never become your alibi,” Gjervik said, stressing that freight traders remain accountable for decisions and that market feel still matters. “Young people today coming into the business, they need to learn how to run a calculation on a piece of paper. Scott Cornell, EVP, Crime and Theft Specialist at SPG Cargo & Logistics and chair of TAPA Americas, describes the process as “laundering freight.” Cross-docks, warehouses, even a parking lot or side street where a load can be transferred, and replacement shipping documents can help disguise where merchandise originated. In some cases, those products can reach overseas markets within days. Cornell worked a case involving a popular headphone brand that showed how quickly stolen merchandise can move. About one week after the theft, the devices began pinging in Europe. That timeline suggested little room between the initial crime and international movement. “They stole it, took it right to the port,” Cornell explained. A warehouse could also provide another stop before products enter a container. Workers can transfer merchandise, create different paperwork and apply another seal. articles.content: Erasmus keeps China boxship spree rolling - Splash247 Athens-based Erasmus Shipinvest has returned to CSSC Huangpu Wenchong for another pair of 1,900 teu containerships, taking its firm programme with the Guangzhou-based builder to eight ships. The John Su-led owner signed the latest contract with the yard and China Shipbuilding Trading this week. The two ships are follow-ons to a pair of the same size contracted in July. Neither price nor delivery dates have been disclosed. The vessels are part of Huangpu Wenchong’s Swan feeder series and measure 172 m long and 27.5 m wide. The design meets IMO EEDI Phase III requirements and comes fitted with shore-power capability and scrubbers. The latest deal builds on a rapid run of contracting between the two companies. Erasmus first signed for two firm plus two optional 1,800 teu ships in April, followed by two further 1,900 teu programmes in June and July. The new pair takes cooperation between Erasmus and Huangpu Wenchong to eight firm ships and six options. Splash covered the July order, when Erasmus’ tally at the yard stood at six firm vessels and six options. The earlier 1,900 teu joint programme was reported at around $32m per ship, although there is no pricing indication yet for the latest pair. Erasmus has been building up both its container and dry bulk orderbooks in China. articles.content: Gulf crude exports rebound sharply - Splash247 Yasa Holding Middle Eastern crude exports have staged a dramatic recovery in September, with tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz rebounding while Saudi Arabia simultaneously restarts its alternative Red Sea export route. Updated Kpler data cited by Reuters put crude exports from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait and Iran at 16.33m barrels per day this month, the highest since the war with Iran began in late February and just under 80% of pre-conflict levels. February exports stood at 19.51m barrels per day. Hormuz flows have recovered particularly sharply. Kpler estimates September crude movements through the strait at around 9.72m barrels per day, including ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, compared with levels as low as 2.2m barrels per day in late July. Saudi Arabia has driven much of the rebound, with exports expected at around 5.4m barrels per day in September, more than double August’s 2.45m barrels per day. Ras Tanura has returned to the centre of Saudi export activity following the September attack on the kingdom’s East-West Pipeline. Shipments from the Gulf terminal have climbed to around 3.25m barrels per day this month from 929,000 barrels per day in August. Kpler counted 19 VLCCs, each carrying roughly 2m barrels of Saudi crude, exiting Hormuz in a single week. articles.content: Seven Island Shipping fleet value passes the half-billion mark - Splash247 Mumbai-based Seven Islands Shipping has emerged as the taker of the 50,000 dwt MTM Mississippi (built 2006), a ship that has been renamed Inspire. A price tag of close to $15.5 m has been attached to the deal.The ship was sold by MT Maritime. The acquisition marks the second MR move this year by the Indian outfit, which is now just one ship short of the 20-vessel mark in the handysize tanker market, a segment in which it has been making waves for years, steadily building up one of the larger MR fleets in South Asia. The Fairfax-backed owner has grown from 14 ships in 2019 to 29 ships in just a handful of years and is now India’s second-largest private tanker shipping company. VesselsValue now puts the fleet’s value at about $612.9m. This year marked the first time Seven Islands’ fleet value passed the half-billion-dollar mark. The company said the agent can reduce the time needed for global trade data research and analysis by up to 90%, depending on the user’s experience and the complexity of the query. The Descartes Datamyne AI Agent is embedded within the company’s global trade intelligence platform and can return answers, visualizations and the underlying shipment records supporting its findings, Descartes said in a Sept. 24 release. The tool is designed to reduce some of the manual work involved in searching Datamyne, allowing users to ask questions without building database filters or learning specific query structures. Users can ask questions about suppliers, buyers, commodities, shipment activity and trade relationships. The agent then analyzes the data and provides contextual answers, along with visualizations and access to the shipment records behind the findings, according to Descartes. Businesses can connect Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or their own internal agents and make requests in plain language. An agent can track shipments, surface exceptions or customs holds, search rates on any lane, or book outright, according to the company. It can submit cargo details, book against negotiated rates, and return a booking ID and transit time without logging into the Flexport platform. The server leads a broader release from the San Francisco-based forwarder, which says more than 13,000 companies use it. The update also extends Flexport Atlas beyond ocean freight and adds customs tools. “The future of global logistics is autonomous: intelligent supply chains that see problems before they happen, calculate the fix, and execute it in a recurring self-improvement loop,” said Ryan Petersen, founder and CEO of Flexport, in the release. articles.content: Geneva Dry unveils expanded agenda for 2027 edition - Splash247 Geneva Dry, the world’s premier annual dry bulk shipping conference, has launched marketing for its 2027 edition with an expanded agenda featuring new sessions on bauxite, investment and crewing, alongside a significantly revamped workshop programme. The fourth edition of Geneva Dry will return to the Hotel President Wilson on the shores of Lake Geneva on April 27 and 28, 2027, bringing together shipowners, charterers, traders, miners, brokers, financiers and technology providers from across the global dry bulk supply chain. The 2027 programme represents a notable evolution from this year’s event with organisers firmly listening to the advice of delegates. Most strikingly, organisers have added a Bauxite Blitz, a dedicated 30-minute examination of one of the fastest-growing seaborne bulk trades. The session will look at expanding bauxite demand, changing sourcing patterns and the implications for dry bulk shipping, with Torvald Klaveness president and CEO Ernst Meyer and South32 charterer and decarbonisation lead Robert Haggquist among those already confirmed. Bauxite joins the established cargo sessions covering minor bulks, agri-commodities, coal and iron ore. articles.content: Trump Denies Offering Iran Sanctions Relief, Tehran Says it is Ready for Talks FILE PHOTO: U.S. President Donald Trump attends an event to sign executive orders in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S., August 6, 2026. REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein/File Photo Trump Denies Offering Iran Sanctions Relief, Tehran Says it is Ready for Talks Reuters Total Views: 0 September 29, 2026 Sept 29 (Reuters) – US President Donald Trump said he has offered Iran nothing to end the war, rejecting media reports that cited US officials saying he was willing to ease sanctions and release frozen funds for “concrete” steps regarding Iran’s nuclear program. “This is untrue. I offered them NOTHING,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Monday. Axios and CNN both reported, citing unidentified US officials, that Trump was willing to give Iran sanctions relief and free Iranian funds as part of a final deal on the condition that Iran showed “concrete progress” on the nuclear issue. Trump has cited preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear bomb as a key goal of the war, along with ending its ability to attack its neighbors and creating conditions for Iranians to topple their leadership. Iran does not have nuclear weapons and denies it wants to develop them, but argues it has the right to a domestic nuclear energy capacity. KKB said the new awards are expected to contribute to earnings and net assets over their respective contract periods. articles.content: Fragmented trade drives dry bulk tonne-mile demand - Splash247 Dry bulk shipping has entered the final quarter of 2026 in considerably better shape than most owners expected, with industry leaders at last week’s Splash Singapore conference arguing that increasingly fragmented trade could keep vessel demand elevated even without spectacular growth in cargo volumes. G2 Ocean chief executive Arthur English admitted the strength of the market had surprised him, particularly in minor bulks where underlying tonnes have barely grown. “All of the growth has come from geopolitical disruptions and delays in ports and so on,” English told the Dry Bulk Market Outlook panel. Norden chief executive Jan Rindbo said he sees something more structural developing. “The world fleet is breaking down into smaller fleets,” he said, pointing to sanctions, Middle Eastern conflicts and European environmental rules determining which ships can participate in individual trades. The result is declining fleet efficiency. “We used to trade as one efficient global fleet,” Rindbo said. “It just means that the world fleet utilisation is coming down.” Pacific Basin chief Martin Fruergaard similarly highlighted the surprising resilience of the world economy despite inflation, high energy prices and geopolitical turmoil. The United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) index gauges a country’s integration into container-shipping networks using factors including vessel calls, port capacity, carrier and service availability, largest ship size and the number of countries reached through direct services. The latest figures underline Asia’s continuing central role in liner shipping. China led the region, while eight Asian economies — South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam, Japan, India, Hong Kong and Taiwan — were among the world’s 15 best-connected economies in the third quarter, UNCTAD said. China’s gap persists China’s connectivity advantage has remained durable since 2023 and increased further through September, UNCTAD said. South Korea and Singapore retained high scores despite modest month-to-month declines, and both remained above their levels a year earlier. The proposed class action lawsuit was filed Sept. 17 in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan by Adis and Denisa Bajgoric, Sasa Susa doing business as ASP Logistics, Mensud Topic, Edin Topic and George Ureche against Red Line Logistics, Zaim Bajgoric and Anel Penava. The case is listed as Bajgoric et al. v. Red Line Logistics Inc. et al., No. 2:26-cv-13533. The class action lawsuit is seeking more than $1 million in damages for plaintiffs. At the center of the complaint is an alleged scheme involving the amount Red Line received from customers for hauling freight and the amount disclosed to owner-operators whose compensation was tied to load revenue. The plaintiffs allege Red Line secured freight from third-party customers and then assigned the loads to owner-operators operating under exclusive lease agreements. Under those agreements, drivers were supposed to receive a percentage of the revenue generated by their loads, minus certain costs and expenses. articles.content: Thieves clone $60K shipment, redirect 41,000 pounds of glycerin in Illinois - FreightWaves Promo Code: FALLFORF3 Limited Quantity Available - Join us at F3: Future of Freight Festival, October 27 & 28th Register Now × A driver hauled 41,336 pounds of glycerin toward Thornton, Illinois, with paperwork that appeared legitimate. Someone had cloned information connected with the $60,000 shipment, according to Cook County investigators. The suspected scheme redirected 75 drums toward a cross-docking operation before anyone transferred the merchandise. Detectives intercepted the semi-truck and secured everything before the cargo disappeared deeper into the supply chain. The load originated in Hammond, Indiana, and traveled toward 16850 Canal Street in Thornton. Each container held 99.7% USP/FCC-grade glycerin, according to information provided by authorities. Intelligence alerted the Organized Retail Crime and Cargo Theft Task Force about the suspected theft. Investigators obtained the bill of lading and immediately began examining details surrounding the delivery. Detectives reviewed carrier information, documentation and the intended destination while tracking the commercial vehicle. Their work led officers to the tractor-trailer after it entered Thornton. Police conducted a traffic stop before anyone could unload or distribute the product. Authorities then secured the merchandise, contacted its lawful owners and coordinated its return. articles.summary:

articles.content: Port of Oakland August volumes fall year over year as exports edge up from July - FreightWaves Promo Code: FALLFORF3 Limited Quantity Available - Join us at F3: Future of Freight Festival, October 27 & 28th Register Now × The Port of Oakland handled 173,818 twenty foot equivalent units (TEUs) in August, with full export volume rising 2.9% from July, although overall loaded-container traffic remained below the prior-year level. Combined loaded imports and exports totaled 131,666 TEUs during the month, down 9% from August 2025. Empty-container traffic, frequently an indicator of future imports, reached 42,152 TEUs, a year-over-year decline of 11.4%, while vessel calls fell to 82 from 90 a year earlier. Year-to-date picture For the first eight months of the year, Oakland’s loaded cargo volume was down 2.5% from the same period in 2025. Full import volume declined 4.6%, partly offset by a 0.2% increase in full exports. Empty-container movements were down 11.4% year to date. The August export gain from July indicates some month-to-month improvement for a gateway that relies heavily on agricultural and other export cargoes. But the year-over-year volume decline points up continuing pressure on the broader import-export market, particularly for second-tier West Coast hubs that have seen carriers concentrate services at LA-Long Beach, and shift some vessel rotations to Canada. articles.content: Contships goes big in China with up to 30 newbuilds - Splash247 Contships Greek feeder specialist Contships Logistics has launched a potentially 30-ship newbuilding programme in China as the Nikolas Pateras-led owner shifts its fleet renewal drive towards fresh tonnage. Wholly owned CLC Newbuildings has signed a letter of intent with Hubei Guangji Green Energy Shipbuilding Group covering 10 firm 1,300 teu containerships plus two sets of 10 options. Pricing and delivery dates have not been disclosed. If all the options are taken up, the newbuilding programme alone would exceed Contships’ existing fleet of 27 feeder vessels. The ships will use the new ContshipMax CV1300 design developed with Shanghai Merchant Ship Design and Research Institute (SDARI). Despite the name, capacity is listed at 1,324 teu, including 340 reefer plugs. The conventionally fuelled vessels will feature Tier III Mitsubishi main engines, low-pressure SCR systems, Daihatsu generators, shaft generators and a package of energy-saving devices. Construction will take place at Guangji’s recently commissioned yard at Wuxue on the Yangtze River, with the Chinese builder working in partnership with Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding & Offshore Project Management. articles.content: UK Sanctions Five LNG Carriers in New Russia Package LNG carrier Alexey Kosygin. Photo courtesy Zvezda Shipbuilding UK Sanctions Five LNG Carriers in New Russia Package Malte Humpert Total Views: 387 October 1, 2026 The United Kingdom has sanctioned five liquefied natural gas carriers as part of a new package of measures targeting Russia’s efforts to expand a maritime “shadow fleet” for LNG exports, including three Russian-built Arc7 ice-class vessels intended to support the Arctic LNG 2 project. The five LNG carriers named in the Oct. 1 sanctions notice are Chaivo, Portovyy, Aleksey Kosygin, Konstantin Posiet and Pyotr Stolypin. The vessels are subject to UK shipping and trade sanctions that prohibit their operation and chartering, bar them from UK ports and restrict the provision and procurement of a broad range of maritime services. The three newest vessels – Aleksey Kosygin, Konstantin Posyet and Pyotr Stolypin – are part of a series of large high ice-class LNG carriers being built for Russia’s Arctic LNG program. Aleksey Kosygin was delivered in December 2025 while Konstantin Posyet followed in June 2026. Pyotr Stolypin was being prepared for sea trials at the Zvezda shipyard in September, according to Russian state oil company Rosneft. London’s sanctioning of Pyotr Stolypin before entering commercial service is noteworthy. articles.content: Transocean-Valaris $5.8bn megadeal clears US antitrust review - Splash247 Valaris Transocean’s $5.8bn takeover of offshore driller Valaris has cleared a key regulatory hurdle in the US, and the companies now expect to complete the transaction in the final quarter of the year. Valaris and Transocean have been notified by the Antitrust Division of the US Department of Justice that it has closed its investigation into the proposed business combination under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act. The clearance removes one of the main regulatory conditions hanging over the all-stock combination. The DOJ had stepped up its review of the transaction in May by issuing both companies with requests for additional information and documentary materials. Transocean and Valaris now expect the deal to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to satisfying or waiving the remaining closing conditions. Under the agreement signed in early February, Switzerland-based Transocean will acquire all outstanding Valaris shares, and Valaris shareholders will receive 15.235 Transocean shares for each share they hold. The deal will leave Transocean shareholders with approximately 53% of the enlarged company on a fully diluted basis, while Valaris shareholders will own about 47%. The combination will create an offshore drilling contractor with an enterprise value of approximately $17bn and one of the largest rig fleets in the sector. Customs proposal raises concerns over border delays, cargo seizures Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is pushing another overhaul of the country’s customs rules that could significantly increase scrutiny of imported goods. While the initiative aims to protect domestic manufacturers from imports that may be entering the country at artificially low values, critics say the proposal could potentially expose cross-border shipments to more inspections, documentation requirements and precautionary seizures. Sheinbaum submitted the proposed amendments to Mexico’s Customs Law, or Ley Aduanera, to the Chamber of Deputies earlier this month as part of the government’s economic package for 2027. The legislation is aimed primarily at combating undervaluation — the practice of declaring imported merchandise below its actual value to reduce duties and taxes. Smith founded Airlink in early 2013 and grew it from a one-person startup into a non-profit organization with nearly $20 million in annual revenue that helps connect humanitarian organizations with airlines to ship relief supplies to disaster areas. A logistics matchmaking organization able to help humanitarian groups coordinate crisis response with the aviation sector had previously not existed. He left the organization in September 2025. During his tenure, Airlink worked with more than 50 airlines and logistics companies, and 250 humanitarian groups across 100 countries, responding to more than 200 disasters and crises, and helping more than 80 million people in need. The fees were suspended for one year beginning Nov. 10, 2025 as part of the U.S.-China economic détente. Under USTR’s governing notice, the pause expires at 11:59 p.m. ET Nov. 9; fees would again become applicable at the start of Nov. 10 unless the agency issues another modification. The measure stems from USTR’s Section 301 investigation into China’s maritime, logistics and shipbuilding policies. It would impose service fees on vessels operated by Chinese companies, Chinese-owned vessels, and, in a separate provision, Chinese-built ships operated by non-Chinese carriers. The original action also established a distinct fee regime for foreign-built vehicle carriers. I said, ‘How many trucks out of this plant? How many trucks do you do?’ I figured they’d say 200 a year; he said, ‘No… 200 a day,’” Trump said according to a transcript of his speech provided by Roll Call. Speaking to Peterbilt workers after touring the facility, Trump highlighted the 25% tariff his administration imposed Nov. 1, 2025, on imported medium- and heavy-duty trucks, along with tariffs on truck parts that do not comply with the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement. Trump pointed to Peterbilt parent PACCAR’s (Nasdaq: PCAR) expansion in Denton as evidence that the policy is working. The Denton factory is a significant piece of PACCAR’s North American manufacturing network. Peterbilt produces medium- and heavy-duty commercial trucks, including Class 8 models, at the North Texas operation. articles.content: Chevron extends Australia asset-integrity deal with EnerMech - Splash247 Chevron UK oilfield services specialist EnerMech has secured a five-year extension to its non-destructive testing contract with Chevron Australia, retaining the inspection and asset-integrity work until the end of 2031. The Aberdeen-headquartered services company first won the assignment in 2017. The renewed agreement covers inspection and integrity support across Chevron Australia’s operations, including major LNG assets in Western Australia. Financial terms were not disclosed. EnerMech has supported Chevron on the Gorgon and Wheatstone LNG projects through commissioning, maintenance, shutdown campaigns, and continuing operational work. Its scope includes advanced non-destructive testing, condition monitoring, corrosion-management services, statutory inspections, engineering support, and specialist integrity work. The extension comes as LNG operators continue to focus on maintaining availability and managing ageing equipment within complex export facilities. Gorgon, located on Barrow Island, and Wheatstone, near Onslow, are among Australia’s largest LNG developments. EnerMech provides a wider range of Australian services across process, pipeline and subsea operations, cranes and lifting, hydraulics, valves, electrical and instrumentation, and integrity management.
